about: Everything a video editor asks before touching a timeline. tools/memory.py stores the answers in memory/brand.json so they are asked once, not every video. 'per_video': true means ask again each time.

questions.q: What is the channel or brand name, and the handle to show on screen?
Where are the logo files (path to SVG or PNG, light and dark versions)?
Brand colours as hex: background, surface, primary text, accent, second accent. Or say 'take them from my old videos' and give the files.
Fonts: one for headings, one for body, one for captions. Free fonts only (Google Fonts or files you own).
Are your graphics light (white cards and canvases) or dark?
Aspect ratio and size?
Frame rate to deliver?
Where does it go (YouTube long form, Shorts, Reels, course)?
Is the footage already colour graded? This skill never grades; grading happens before the edit.
What resolution was the camera footage shot in? (4K source on a 1080p timeline allows 2x punch-ins without softness.)
One camera or several angles? If several, how are they synced?
Do you supply screen recordings, b-roll or screenshots, and where are they? May the editor use free stock or screenshots of pages you mention?
How tight should the cut be?
Remove every filler word (um, uh, like, you know) or only the distracting ones?
When a line was said more than once, keep the last take unless told otherwise?
Anything that must never be cut (jokes, tangents, sponsor reads, disclaimers)?
How much camera movement on the talking head?
options: always moving - slow push on every shot plus punch-ins

questions.q: Largest punch-in allowed (for example 1.3 = 130 %)?
What kind of motion graphics do you use?
Do you use 3D?
Where do graphics sit?
How often? (roughly how many seconds of pure talking head before something appears)
Anything you never want (memes, stock footage, emojis, AI images, particular colours)?
Captions?
If captions are on: position, upper or lower case, highlight colour for the active or key word?
Background music?
options: quiet bed all the way through
only under intros, graphics and transitions

questions.q: What mood or genre, or a track you already use? (Free libraries only unless you supply the file.)
Sound effects?
options: subtle - soft clicks and whooshes on graphics
punchy - every cut and pop is heard

questions.q: Loudness target (YouTube normalises to -14 LUFS)?
Recurring pieces: intro sting, lower third with your name, chapter title cards, subscribe prompt, end screen. Which do you want and do you have assets?
Which saved style should this follow (see memory/styles), or do you have new reference videos or old videos of your own to learn from?
Three things you have hated in past edits?
